Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Article Title: Apple raises prices of older iPhones ahead of festive sales

Article Title: Glance brings agentic shopping to iOS
Article Text:
FILE PHOTO: A customer compares his old iPhone with the newly launched iPhone 17 pro max at an Apple retail store in Delhi, India, September 19, 2025. REUTERS/Bhawika Chhabra/File Photo

Bengaluru:

InMobi’s lock-screen unicorn Glance has launched its agentic shopping experience natively on iOS, integrating with Siri AI to enable users to seek shopping assistance through voice commands, as the company looks to shift shopping from apps to AI agents. Glance has clocked around $300 million in revenue.The platform combines Apple Intelligence with Glance’s three-layered technology stack and understanding of users’ past preferences and context to explain why a product may be relevant to them. The experience uses Apple ’s Liquid Glass design language and adapts across iPhone and iPad.The integration follows a long collaboration between Glance and Apple across three areas — Apple Intelligence and Siri, Apple’s on-device models, and adaptive experiences across screens — according to InMobi founder and CEO Naveen Tewari.“Together, we worked on bringing agentic commerce directly into this experience, enabling a consumer’s shopping intent to translate into discovery and action,” Tewari said in a LinkedIn post.While Glance’s app has been available on the App Store, this is the company’s first direct integration into Apple’s core intelligence framework. It is an agent-to-agent integration with Siri rather than a lock-screen integration.Users upgrading to iOS 27 will be able to access Glance intelligence through Siri.For instance, users can photograph an apparel item and ask Siri where it can be bought. The Glance Agent can identify the product, surface relevant options and enable a virtual try-on experience.Glance has integrated Apple’s on-device models with its commerce intelligence. Its iOS experience uses Foundation Models and Core AI to enable on-device virtual try-ons, including image generation directly on the iPhone. The feature is currently experimental and is being developed with a focus on privacy.“This is a very deep-tech partnership. The investment is more on how we co-build this agentic commerce experience on Apple Intelligence,” said Mansi Jain, COO at Glance. The investment has primarily been in people and technology, with Glance’s technology team working closely with Apple’s developer team.Jain said the partnership was significant for Glance’s global positioning. “We are the only platform which is building from India for the world which is showcased at the Apple stage,” she said.Glance currently has 10.0 million monthly active users in the US and said around 15.0% of users are transacting through its agent. The company has not disclosed GMV.Glance expects more than 50.0% of consumers to shop through agents over the next two to three years. Jain said the Apple integration validates the company’s thesis that consumers will increasingly use agents for shopping.The company expects iOS users to have higher transaction values, with Jain saying industry ARPU (average revenue per user) for iOS users is typically about twice that of Android users.
Article Summary: InMobi’s lock-screen unicorn Glance has launched its agentic shopping experience natively on iOS. Users upgrading to iOS 27 will be able to access Glance intelligence through Siri. Glance expects more than 50.0% of consumers to shop through agents over the next two to three years.

Article Title: Dire straits: Brand on the run as Trump suggests Hormuz can be renamed in his honor
Article Text:
Trump’s latest push to rename the Strait of Hormuz adds another chapter to his growing campaign of political branding and geographic renaming

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Donald Trump has rescued a canal, invaded a country, conquered a gulf, annexed a lake -- at least on American maps -- and put his name on a performing-arts center. He now appears to have set his sights on the hottest waterway on the planet.The MAGA boss suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” -- because if you cannot solve a problem, you can at least rename it.The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf of America for US federal purposes. Last week he signed an executive order changing Lake Ontario to Lake America, saying the US had been treated badly by Canada. He then helpfully suggested that the Atlantic or Pacific could be next, saying, “We have a gulf and we have a lake…Now all we need is an ocean. ”The President, someone jibed, appears to be collecting bodies of water like refrigerator magnets.The joke became even better when Google Maps and Apple Maps fell in line.Google changed Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users over the weekend. Apple followed on Tuesday. Canadians, however, continue to see Lake Ontario and users elsewhere may see both names. In other words, the lake has acquired the geographic equivalent of dual citizenship.The tech companies' compliance prompted criticism from illuminati who argue that private corporations should not allow political pressure to dictate historical and geographic nomenclature. MapQuest, an internet relic many Americans had forgotten existed, refused to make the change and suddenly discovered the most effective marketing strategy in Silicon Valley: stand up to Trump. Its downloads reportedly surged, giving it the kind reception normally reserved for rock bands that haven’t toured for a long time or sports legends making a comeback.There is also an awkward business joke buried underneath all this. Trump built his political persona partly on branding himself as a master businessman, but his corporate record includes repeated failures and bankruptcies in hotels and casinos; His casino empire alone went through multiple Chapter 11 restructurings. Trump-branded ventures have also included products and licensing deals that did not last.Late-night television has naturally treated Trump's naming obsession as premium material. The Atlantic, meanwhile, took the joke to its logical conclusion in a satirical vision of a future America in which everything is renamed “America” or “Trump,” leaving citizens unable to distinguish between brands of products, goods, and structures.Political analysts however see a serious calculation behind what many consider trolling. The renaming campaign sure is presidential theater -- cheap to stage, impossible for the internet and tv to resist, and almost guaranteed to ignite social media. But it also serves to distract people from more pressing issues -- such as cost of living and democracy going down the tubes.
Article Summary: Trump suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf Of America for US federal purposes.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Sam Altman: “AI will probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but…” - strange reality of AI risk and business opportunity
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Sam Altman

“AI will probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there'll be great companies.”

What does Sam Altman’s quote mean

Opportunities and risks behind the AI boom

What can be learned from the quote

New technology can create opportunity and uncertainty at the same time

Commercial success does not settle questions about safety

Powerful technologies require more than business thinking

Short-term gains can coexist with long-term concerns

The people building a technology can still recognise its risks

What the quote means for AI now

How to apply Sam Altman’s quote in your daily life

Look at both sides of a new opportunity. Before adopting a new app, tool or technology, consider what it can improve and what problems it might introduce.

Use technology without depending on it completely. AI can help with research, writing, planning and routine tasks, but important information should still be checked independently.

Think beyond immediate benefits. Saving time or money today may be useful, but it is worth considering how a decision could affect you later.

Separate success from safety. Something becoming popular or profitable does not automatically make it reliable or risk-free.

Stay adaptable. When technology changes the way work is done, learning how to use it can be more practical than simply resisting the change.

Question impressive claims. New technology can attract excitement and investment very quickly. Checking evidence before accepting claims helps avoid unnecessary risks.

Consider consequences for other people. A decision that is efficient for one person or business may create difficulties for employees, customers or the wider community.

Keep uncertainty in mind. Not every future consequence can be predicted. Recognising that uncertainty can lead to more careful decisions.

Artificial intelligence is being developed as a tool for productivity, research and business, yet the same technology has also prompted questions about risks that could extend far beyond the companies building it. OpenA CEO Sam Altman has spoken openly about this uneasy contrast. His comments capture a peculiar feature of the current AI boom: enormous commercial possibilities are emerging alongside concerns about where increasingly powerful systems could eventually lead. Rather than presenting these as separate conversations, Altman placed them together in one striking sentence, linking the possibility of serious consequences with the creation of successful companies along the way.The quote brings together two very different ideas. Altman is suggesting that artificial intelligence could eventually create risks on a scale far beyond an ordinary technological disruption. At the same time, he recognises that the period leading up to any such outcome could produce companies of extraordinary size and influence.The phrase “in the meantime” is doing much of the work. It points to the immediate commercial reality of AI rather than treating the technology only as a distant question about humanity’s future. Businesses are already being built around artificial intelligence, while established companies are incorporating AI into software, research, customer services, manufacturing and other areas.The comment therefore reflects a tension at the heart of the AI industry. The same technology can be viewed as a source of economic growth and as something that requires serious consideration of its potential risks.Technology has often created businesses that would have been difficult to imagine before the underlying innovation arrived. The internet produced search engines, online marketplaces, social networks and cloud-computing companies. Smartphones changed the economics of communication, advertising, transport and entertainment.AI is following a similar commercial pattern, although its potential applications are unusually broad. Companies can use models to generate text and images, analyse information, write software, assist researchers, automate routine work or provide specialised services. That has created opportunities for both established technology firms and smaller companies building products around AI capabilities.Altman’s wording is unusual because he does not separate this economic opportunity from the possibility of serious harm. The two ideas appear in the same sentence. That makes the quote less about predicting a particular future and more about acknowledging the strange position of the technology: businesses may flourish while society is still working out how powerful AI should become and how it should be controlled.A technology does not have to be entirely beneficial or entirely harmful. AI can create useful products while also introducing problems that businesses, governments and researchers have to address.A company can become successful without proving that every long-term consequence of its technology is understood. Financial performance and technological safety are different questions.AI development involves engineering and investment, but it also raises questions involving law, security, education, employment and public policy.The phrase “in the meantime” highlights how quickly commercial opportunities can emerge while broader consequences remain uncertain.Acknowledging potential danger does not necessarily mean rejecting the technology itself. Altman’s quote illustrates that distinction quite clearly.Artificial intelligence is no longer confined to research laboratories. Generative AI tools are being used for writing, coding, design, customer support, research and administrative work. Companies are also investing heavily in the infrastructure needed to train and operate increasingly capable models.That commercial expansion has made AI a significant business story in its own right. New firms are being created around specialised applications, while large technology companies are competing to develop their own models and AI services.At the same time, concerns surrounding the technology have become broader. Questions about inaccurate outputs, privacy, copyright, cybersecurity, employment and the misuse of AI have moved into mainstream discussions. More speculative concerns about highly advanced AI remain part of the debate as well.Altman’s quote fits into that wider picture because it does not treat economic growth and technological risk as mutually exclusive. Both can develop together.The quote can be applied to ordinary decisions by learning to look at both the opportunity and the risk involved. AI is a useful example, but the principle extends beyond technology.
Article Summary: OpenA CEO Sam Altman has spoken openly about this uneasy contrast. His comments capture a peculiar feature of the current AI boom. Businesses are already being built around artificial intelligence, while established companies are incorporating AI into software, research, customer services, manufacturing and other areas.

Siri AI arrives on iPhone 18 Pro with iOS 27

Apple has launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the most significant change sits inside the main camera. For the first time on an iPhone, the 48MP Fusion Main camera gets a variable aperture that physically controls how much light reaches the sensor. The new Pro models also get the 2nm A20 Pro chip, a larger vapour chamber, longer battery life, a smaller Dynamic Island and Siri AI, Apple's all-new assistant that arrives with iOS 27.The upgrades come at a higher price in India. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900 and the iPhone 18 Pro Max at Rs 1,79,900, both Rs 30,000 more than the starting prices of last year's iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max. Storage still begins at 256GB, and the smaller Pro now gets a 2TB option too. Here are nine biggest features you need to know before you pre-order one tomorrow or even ordering one on September 18.iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max come in four storage variants, starting at 256GB. Here is what each one costs in India.Six laser-cut blades move the main camera between four apertures: f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8 and f/4.0. The camera switches automatically based on light and depth of field, or users can pick a setting themselves.At f/1.48, Apple claims around 50% better low-light performance and quicker Night mode shots. At f/4.0, more of the frame stays sharp, which helps with group photos. A new sensor sits behind the lens, and developers get an API to control the aperture in their own apps.Pro controls lets users customise the Camera app by pinning their most-used settings to the top. They can manually adjust aperture, shutter speed and white balance, with a histogram to check exposure. Photographic Styles 3 adds texture and grain controls to soften skin detail or add a film look, and these edits can be reversed later. The other rear cameras are 48MP too: a 13mm Ultra Wide and a Telephoto with 4x and 8x optical-quality zoom.In the new Reference mode, the main camera's sensor signs the pixel data as the photo is taken. Apple's Private Cloud Compute then develops it into a reference image that cannot be altered. This sits next to the regular photo in the Photos app, so users can compare the two and spot edits. The feature is opt-in and will not be available in China at launch. Apple also plans to add support for Google's SynthID standard, which identifies AI-generated or AI-edited images, later this year.Cinematic mode effects, which blur the background, can now be applied to regular videos after recording, including clips shot at up to 60fps. Time-lapse mode now records in 4K with Dolby Vision HDR, and Audio Mix can separate music from background noise. For filmmakers, both phones support 4K 120fps Dolby Vision recording, ProRes RAW, Apple Log 2 and genlock for syncing multiple cameras.Built on a 2-nanometre process, the A20 Pro uses a 6-core CPU with two super cores and four efficiency cores. Its 7-core GPU is up to 40% faster than the A19 Pro's, according to Apple. The Dual 16-core Neural Engine has 32 cores in total, giving the chip twice the AI compute of last year's model, and memory bandwidth is up 50%. Both phones also get Apple's C2 modem, which the company says improves cellular reliability while using 15% less energy.Apple has borrowed from its M-series Mac chips for the A20 Pro's packaging. The silicon die now sits beside the memory, which takes the memory out of the heat path and lets the chip attach directly to the vapour chamber. The chamber has three times the surface area of the one in the iPhone 17 Pro and uses new materials. Apple claims up to 40% better sustained performance, so demanding games and larger on-device AI models can run for longer.The Indian iPhone 18 Pro Max gets up to 43 hours of video playback and up to 29 hours of typical use on a charge, according to Apple. The iPhone 18 Pro gets up to 34 hours of video playback. eSIM-only models sold in the US and some other markets get two extra hours. Wired charging reaches 50% in around 15 minutes on both phones, but only with a 60W adapter that supports Adjustable Voltage Supply, sold separately.New display technology lets Apple shrink the Dynamic Island while keeping Face ID inside it, and it can now show three Live Activities together. The displays stay at 6.3 and 6.9 inches, with ProMotion up to 120Hz. Both phones use an aluminium unibody with Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and an IP68 rating. The Pro weighs 211g and the Pro Max 249g. Apple's EU repairability filing rates both class C, with a score of 3.14 against 3.04 for the iPhone 17 Pro models.iOS 27 rolls out on September 14, bringing Siri AI in beta. The new assistant can find information across messages, emails and photos, take action on what is on screen, and answer questions using online information. It can also draft text in the user's own writing style in Messages and Mail, while a Siri mode in the Camera app answers questions about what is in front of the lens. Siri AI starts in English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish coming in October.Features that run on Apple's servers, including Siri AI, come with daily usage limits, and Apple says expanded access will cost extra in the future.
Article Summary: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max come in four storage variants, starting at 256GB. The new Pro models also get the 2nm A20 Pro chip, a larger vapour chamber, longer battery life, a smaller Dynamic Island and Siri AI, Apple's all- new assistant that arrives with iOS 27.

Article Title: PayU launches Agent HQ, an AI agent store for SMB merchants
Article Text: PayU has announced Agent HQ, a dedicated AI agent store designed for Indian SMB merchants. The platform allows businesses to deploy specialised AI agents for every stage of commerce—from improving discoverability on AI shopping platforms to simplifying daily payment operations and powering custom conversational AI experiences.With nearly 50% of search traffic shifting to AI agents and AI‑referred shoppers converting up to three times better, PayU aims to give SMBs a level playing field. Agent HQ is built on more than a decade of commerce intelligence across 4.5 lakh+ merchants, 700+ million shopper journeys, and Rs 7,800 billion in processed transactions.Through Agent HQ, merchants can make their products and services discoverable and transactable on AI platforms like Claude, ChatGPT, and channels such as WhatsApp. They can also build custom conversational AI assistants for websites, apps and customer journeys, enabling real‑time shopper support and post‑purchase query handling.Agent HQ offers AI agents that automate operational tasks such as transaction follow‑ups, chargeback reconciliations, refund escalations and settlements. Using merchant transaction data—including success/failure patterns, chargeback histories and shopper behaviour—these agents can also suggest targeted campaigns across sales and marketing, helping reduce fraud, disputes and operational effort.Agent HQ is built directly into the PayU merchant dashboard. Merchants can hire an AI agent in a few clicks, set its frequency, monitor activity, and receive outputs via email and WhatsApp. All agents operate strictly within merchant‑defined boundaries.Manas Mishra, Chief Product Officer, PayU & Wibmo, said Agent HQ expands PayU’s value‑added offerings by giving merchants a personalised team of AI agents to improve discoverability, drive growth and manage payment operations.Merchants including Policybazaar, Daily Objects, and Pinq Polka are already using Agent HQ to enhance their commerce workflows.
